land.text: the Kaveri delta around Thanjavur, taken by Venkoji (Ekoji I) in 1675-1676

predecessors.note: Pages disagree: the Thanjavur Nayak page says the Nayak kingdom was 'disestablished: 1673' (siege by Chokkanatha of Madurai) and 'Madurai briefly ruled the city till 1675 when the Maratha general Venkoji (Ekoji I) captured Thanjavur'; the Maratha page's infobox gives April 1674 for the conquest and its text 'early 1676'. Cliopatria's Nayaks of Thanjavur row ends in 1676.

land.text: 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company' under the Treaty of 1799

successors.note: Serfoji II kept 'limited authority over the Thanjavur Fort and its immediate surroundings', a fifth of the land revenue and a pension; the principality was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse after Shivaji died in October 1855.

rulers.name: Thuljaji
rulers.note: Deposed in 1773 when the Nawab's and the Company's troops occupied Thanjavur; reinstated 1776.

rulers.name: Serfoji II
rulers.note: Adopted 23 January 1787, under the regent Amar Singh, who 'usurped the throne in 1793' (Serfoji II page).

rulers.name: Serfoji II (restored)
rulers.note: Restored by the British on 23 June 1798; the Treaty of 1799 transferred the administration; he lived to 1832 as the 'last sovereign ruler' and titular maharaja.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1677, but Venkoji 'occupied Thanjavur and assumed sovereign power in early 1676'. Same shape, one year earlier.

correction.text: the Kaveri delta kingdom, shape unchanged, valid from 1676

keyframe_review.note: 14,694 km2 (49 cells, 78.6-79.8 E, 10.0-11.3 N): the Kaveri delta. The page gives no area ('the kingdom governed the Kaveri delta') so no ratio. The shape's northern edge is the Kollidam river itself (its northmost cells are the river's own cells), which matches the page: during Shivaji's 1677 expedition Venkoji 'assigned territory north of the Kollidam river to his commander Santaji', so no further loss is needed in the ledger. Valid 1677-1699.

14,104 km2: two cells at the Kaveri/Kollidam split near Tiruchirappalli (78.75-79.2 E, 10.93-11.08 N) drop out. No page opened dates a cession there (the page names only tribute: 'Shahuji I paid annual tribute to Mughal commanders' during the siege of Jinji); a 4% change, kept. Unverified in detail.
14,610 km2: three cells return along the north (78.75-79.68 E, 10.93-11.39 N). No page opened dates it; 3.6% change.

14,313 km2 for 1738-1798: two northern cells (79.2-79.68 E, 11.08-11.39 N) drop out again, the Kollidam side. The shape holds through the 1762 tribute treaty and the 1773-1776 occupation by the Nawab and the Company: they changed who controlled the kingdom, not its extent, and the ledger records them. No page gives the 1738 year for any border move.

Last year of the shape (14,313 km2). Under the Treaty of 1799 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company'; Serfoji kept limited authority over the fort and its surroundings, so the map should draw the kingdom as British from 1800.

ledger.note: 1676: Venkoji (Ekoji I), half-brother of Shivaji, makes himself king at Thanjavur. 'The Bijapur Sultan sent Venkoji in 1675. After defeating Alagiri at Ayyampet, he occupied Thanjavur and assumed sovereign power in early 1676', founding the Bhonsle dynasty. The sources differ (1674, 1675, 1676); the Nayak page: 'Madurai briefly ruled the city till 1675 when the Maratha general Venkoji (Ekoji I) captured Thanjavur'.

1762: Thanjavur becomes tributary to the Nawab of Arcot. 'In 1762, British mediation resulted in a tripartite treaty that imposed a fixed annual tribute payable by Thanjavur to the Nawab of Arcot.' 'This placed the kingdom in polical subordination' (sic). Mirror of carnatic-sultanate's vassal_start of 1762 (added by reviewer sa-05-d).

region.text: the kingdom, tributary to the Nawab of Arcot

ledger.note: 1773: 'troops of the Nawab and the East India Company occupied Thanjavur', and Thuljaji was deposed. The 1762 tripartite treaty had already fixed a tribute 'payable to the Nawab of Arcot', in the Carnatic dossier as a vassal relation. Typed as an occupation (reviewer sa-05-d): the page says the Nawab's and the Company's troops 'occupied Thanjavur' and the king was 'deposed until the court of directors ordered his reinstatement in 1776', so the land was held, not annexed; mirrors carnatic-sultanate's occupation_start of 1773.
1776: Thuljaji is reinstated 'on condition of hosting a British subsidiary garrison'. Typed as the end of the 1773 occupation (reviewer sa-05-d); mirrors carnatic-sultanate's occupation_end of 1776.

1799: the tributary relation to the Nawab ends when the kingdom passes to the Company. 'Under the treaty of 1799, Serfoji ceded civil and military administration to the Company.' The page does not say the tribute ended then; the year is the treaty's. Mirror of carnatic-sultanate's vassal_end of 1799 (added by reviewer sa-05-d).

region.text: the kingdom, no longer the Nawab's tributary

ledger.note: 1799: Serfoji II signs the Treaty of 1799 and 'the administration of the Thanjavur kingdom was transferred entirely to the British East India Company'. Restored by the British on 23 June 1798 after Amar Singh's usurpation of 1793. The principality survived on paper until 1855 (Doctrine of Lapse), which the map does not draw.

region.text: the kingdom's administration, transferred to the Company

wars.name: Shivaji's southern (Karnataka) expedition

zones.text: the Kollidam frontier, territory north of it

wars.outcome: Shivaji seized Gingee and advanced to the Kaveri; Venkoji negotiated and assigned the land north of the Kollidam to his commander Santaji. The Shivaji page adds that on 26 November 1677 Shivaji beat his half-brother's army and seized most of his possessions on the Mysore plateau, and that a settlement later returned many properties to Venkoji's family.
wars.note: The page does not name a 'Treaty with Ekoji'.

wars.name: Carnatic Wars
wars.outcome: Pratapsingh allied with Muhammad Ali Khan Wallajah and the East India Company against the French; no change to Thanjavur's extent is on the page. The 1762 tripartite treaty, mediated by the British, fixed an annual tribute to the Nawab of Arcot.

wars.name: Occupation of Thanjavur by the Nawab and the Company
wars.outcome: Thanjavur was occupied in 1773 and Thuljaji deposed; he was reinstated in 1776 with a British garrison.

certainty.note: The pages give a kingdom of the Kaveri delta but no boundary and no area; the only river line named is the Kollidam (1677), which is also the northern edge of the shape.

sources.title: Thanjavur Maratha kingdom
sources.note: Founding, rulers, 1677 expedition, 1762 tribute, 1773-1776 occupation, 1799 treaty, 1855.

sources.title: Thanjavur Nayak kingdom
sources.note: End of the Nayak kingdom (1673 siege) and Venkoji's capture of Thanjavur by 1675.

sources.title: Shivaji
sources.note: 26 November 1677 defeat of Venkoji's army and seizure of his Mysore-plateau possessions (also used in maratha-empire).

notes:
Three new pages (Thanjavur Maratha kingdom, Serfoji II, Thanjavur Nayak kingdom) plus the Shivaji page also opened for maratha-empire; budget up to 5.

Founding date: the pages give 1673-1674 (conquest of the Madurai Nayak kingdom by Venkoji, April 1674, infobox), 1675 (lead; the Nayak page) and early 1676 (text). 1676 is used: the year the text says Venkoji 'assumed sovereign power'.

End date: Cliopatria ends the row in 1799; the Serfoji II page says the Treaty of 1799 transferred the administration entirely to the Company and calls Serfoji the 'last sovereign ruler', but gives no month; the infobox disestablishes the principality in 1855. 1799 is used; the 1855 Doctrine of Lapse annexation is not drawn.

Not settled: (1) the Kollidam land assigned in 1677: the Cliopatria shape already stops at the river, so no event is recorded, but whether it was a cession to Shivaji or a delegation to Santaji is not clear from the page; (2) the 2-3 cell differences between the Cliopatria shapes of 1677, 1700, 1713 and 1738, which no page opened dates (the Mughal tribute at the siege of Jinji, the 1713 independence of the Carnatic and the 1736 Madurai annexation by the Carnatic are the likely causes, not in the pages opened); (3) Mysore invasions: the page mentions one invasion repulsed by Venkoji and Chokkanatha without a date or Hyder Ali, and is silent on a 1771 Nawab siege and 1780 (so no ledger event); (4) the page does not say that Nagapattinam, Devikottai or Karaikal were ceded; (5) the vassal relations (tribute to the Mughals during the siege of Jinji, 1762 tribute to the Nawab of Arcot) are in carnatic-sultanate's ledger, not here.

Counterparts needing a dossier: none beyond those of other batches (nayaks-of-thanjavur, carnatic-sultanate, maratha-empire, british-empire).
